hook: A monochrome still image from a U.S. military sensor system, submitted by the FBI to AARO, showing one to two small dark objects positioned just above and to the right of a central crosshair reticle against a grainy background.
why_it_matters: This image is notable because the original military imagery was redacted before reaching AARO, meaning the disclosure pipeline itself introduced information loss prior to government analysis — a chain-of-custody gap that limits independent assessment. The operator's documented inability to positively identify the objects, combined with a corrupted system timestamp, removes two of the most basic evidentiary anchors (identity and time) from what should be a controlled military observation. The absence of any accompanying mission report means sensor parameters, altitude, heading, and operational context are entirely unknown.
key_findings: The image originated from a U.S. military system and was routed through the FBI to AARO as part of the formal UAP reporting pipeline.
Redactions were applied to the original imagery before submission to AARO, not after — meaning AARO itself received a pre-filtered version of the military sensor data.
The operator who captured the imagery reported being unable to positively identify the UAP, indicating the object did not match known signatures at time of observation.
The date displayed in the image is incorrect due to the system's date/time not being configured properly, making temporal correlation with other events or sensor logs unreliable.
No accompanying mission report was provided, leaving all operational context — including sensor type, platform, altitude, speed, and geographic precision — absent from the record.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The image was formally submitted to AARO through the FBI as part of the PURSUE disclosure process, placing it directly within AARO's UAP intake and resolution mission.

The imagery originates from an unspecified U.S. military system, suggesting a connection to military sensor infrastructure and the broader defense UAP data collection apparatus historically centered at Wright-Patterson.
